sample.conclusion: Per-asset type key selects descriptor index 515; field classRef selects descriptor index 539. Repeated names trigger provisionality warnings but neither selection uses a name-hash lookup.

comparisonAudit.baseline: random 1.4.2.5 raw EBX assets compared with Frosty XML
comparisonAudit.savedSummarySays: All 14 disagreements involve type names with more than one layout; decoder uses the asset type key, Frosty uses its SDK class.
comparisonAudit.missingEvidence: The saved summary has no asset paths, type keys, descriptor indices, or field-level diff for the 14 cases. The cases were not rerun in this review.

decision: Keep duplicate-name warnings. They are conservatism for unresolved same-name layouts, not evidence of a selection ambiguity in this 1.4.3.0 type-key map.
recommendedRegression: Construct two descriptor classes with the same name hash but unique type keys and distinct fields. Assert each top-level key selects its own descriptor, nested structures follow the explicit classRef index, and both decoded objects retain the ambiguity marker. Add a guard for duplicate type keys because dictionary construction otherwise overwrites an entry.
limits: One representative M4A1 object chain was re-decoded; this is not a complete layout audit.
The 14 prior XML disagreement records were unavailable in itemized form and were not rerun.
Layout correctness does not establish field semantics, weapon-timing composition, activation, or runtime mechanics.
